displayedInputs.question:
Use 2 triangles and 1 square to make a picture. How many shapes are used altogether? Calculate: \(2+1=?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-1)

What is true of the opposite sides of a rectangle?

[Figure 1](attached-image-2)

choices.A: Opposite sides are equal in length
choices.B: All four sides have different lengths

displayedInputs.question:
What is true of the four sides of a square?

[Figure 1](attached-image-3)

choices.A: All four sides are equal in length
choices.B: Only opposite sides are equal in length

displayedInputs.question:
How does a right angle compare with an acute angle?

[Figure 1](attached-image-4)

choices.A: A right angle is larger than an acute angle
choices.B: A right angle is smaller than an acute angle
choices.C: A right angle and an acute angle are equal in size

displayedInputs.question:
How does an obtuse angle compare with a right angle?

[Figure 1](attached-image-5)

choices.A: An obtuse angle is larger than a right angle
choices.B: An obtuse angle is smaller than a right angle
choices.C: An obtuse angle is equal to a right angle

displayedInputs.question:
What is true of the opposite sides of a parallelogram?

[Figure 1](attached-image-6)

choices.A: Opposite sides are parallel and equal in length
choices.B: None of the four sides are parallel

displayedInputs.question:
A trapezoid has only what feature?

[Figure 1](attached-image-7)

choices.A: One pair of parallel opposite sides
choices.B: All four sides equal in length

displayedInputs.question:
What can be said about the shapes seen when viewing the same object from the front, side, and top?

[Figure 1](attached-image-8)

choices.A: The shapes seen may be different
choices.B: The shape must be the same
choices.C: Only the front can be seen
